title: Incorrect Flow
statementMd:
At the entrance examination for the magistracy of the MSU Cyber-Mechanics Department Sasha got the question about Ford-Fulkerson algorithm. He knew the topic perfectly as he worked with it many times on programming competition. As the task for the question he was given a network with partially build flow that he had to use in order to demonstrate the workflow of the algorithm. He quickly finished to write the text and took a look at the problem only to understand that the given network is incorrect!

Suppose you are given a directed graph $*G*(*V*, *E*)$ with two special nodes $*s*$ and $*t*$ called source and sink. We denote as $*n*$ the number of nodes in the graph, i.e. $*n* = |*V*|$ and $*m*$ stands for the number of directed edges in the graph, i.e. $*m* = |*E*|$. For the purpose of this problem we always consider node $1$ to be the source and node $*n*$ to be the sink. In addition, for each edge of the graph $*e*$ we define the capacity function $*c*(*e*)$ and flow function $*f*(*e*)$. Function $*f*(*e*)$ represents the correct flow if the following conditions are satisfied:

1. For each edge ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6993d107566a95920211ffa5fd9ac68603c00165.png) the flow is non-negative and does not exceed capacity $*c*(*e*)$, i.e. $0 ≤ *f*(*e*) ≤ *c*(*e*)$.
2. For each node ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bba1fc2f81d8879b4f45b8874c136db6be494079.png), that is not source or sink ($*v* ≠ *s*$ and $*v* ≠ *t*$) the sum of flows of all edges going in $*v*$ is equal to the sum of the flows among all edges going out from $*v*$. In other words, there is no flow stuck in $*v*$.

It was clear that as the exam was prepared last night and there are plenty of mistakes in the tasks. Sasha asked one of the professors to fix the network or give the correct task, but the reply was that the magistrate student should be able to fix the network himself. As the professor doesn't want the task to become easier, he asks Sasha to fix the network in a such way that the total number of changes is minimum possible. Sasha is not allowed to remove edges, add new ones or reverse the direction of existing edges. The only thing he is able to do is to change capacity function $*c*(*e*)$ and flow function $*f*(*e*)$. Moreover, all the values should remain non-negative integers. There is no requirement on the flow to be maximum in any sense.

Find the minimum possible total change of the functions $*f*(*e*)$ and $*c*(*e*)$ that Sasha has to make in order to make the flow correct. The total change is defined as the sum of absolute differences, i.e. if new functions are $*f*^{ * }(*e*)$ and $*c*^{ * }(*e*)$, then the total change is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d0231fd13acfe49406e89c890aa30b986fdfee4f.png).

## Input

The first line of the input contains two integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$, $0 ≤ *m* ≤ 100$) — the number of nodes and edges in the graph respectively. Each of the following $*m*$ lines contains the description of the edges, consisting of four integers $*u*_{*i*}$, $*v*_{*i*}$, $*c*_{*i*}$ and $*f*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$, $*u*_{*i*} ≠ *v*_{*i*}$, $0 ≤ *c*_{*i*}, *f*_{*i*} ≤ 1 000 000$) — index of the node the edges starts from, the index of the node the edge goes to, current capacity and flow value.

Node number $1$ is the source, and node number $*n*$ is the sink. It's guaranteed that no edge goes to the source, and no edges starts in the sink.

Given graph contains no self-loops but may contain multiple edges.

## Output

Print one integer — the minimum total sum of changes that Sasha has to do in order to get the correct flow description.

## Note

In the first sample, the flow is initially correct. Note, that the flow is not maximum, but this is not required.

In the second sample, the flow value of the only edge is greater than its capacity. There are two ways to fix this: either increase the capacity up to $2$ or reduce the flow down to $1$.

In the third sample, there is only $1$ unit of flow coming to vertex $2$, but there are $2$ units going out of it. One of the possible solutions is to reduce the value of the flow on the second edge by $1$.

In the fourth sample, there is isolated circulation of flow, but this description is correct by definition.
statementZhMd:
在 MSU 网络力学系的硕士入学考试中，Sasha 遇到了关于 Ford-Fulkerson 算法的问题。由于他在程序设计竞赛中多次使用过该算法，因此对这个主题非常熟悉。作为题目的一部分，他拿到了一张带有部分流的网络，需要利用它来演示算法的执行过程。他很快写完了文字说明，但看了一眼题目后发现，给出的网络竟然是错误的！

假设给定一个有向图 $*G*(*V*, *E*)$，其中有两个特殊节点 $*s*$ 和 $*t*$，分别称为源点和汇点。我们用 $*n*$ 表示图中节点的数量，即 $*n* = |*V*|$，用 $*m*$ 表示图中有向边的数量，即 $*m* = |*E*|$。在本题中，我们始终将节点 $1$ 视为源点，将节点 $*n*$ 视为汇点。此外，对于图中的每条边 $*e*$，我们定义容量函数 $*c*(*e*)$ 和流函数 $*f*(*e*)$。如果满足以下条件，则函数 $*f*(*e*)$ 表示一个正确的流：

1. 对于每条边 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6993d107566a95920211ffa5fd9ac68603c00165.png)，流量非负且不超过容量 $*c*(*e*)$，即 $0 ≤ *f*(*e*) ≤ *c*(*e*)$。
2. 对于每个既不是源点也不是汇点的节点 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bba1fc2f81d8879b4f45b8874c136db6be494079.png)（$*v* ≠ *s*$ 且 $*v* ≠ *t*$），所有进入 $*v*$ 的边上的流量之和等于所有从 $*v*$ 离开的边上的流量之和。换句话说，流量不能在 $*v*$ 处滞留。

显然，由于考试是在前一天晚上准备的，题目中存在许多错误。Sasha 请求一位教授修正网络，或者重新出一道正确的题目，但教授回答说，硕士生应该能够自行修正网络。由于教授不希望题目变得更简单，他要求 Sasha 以总修改次数尽可能少的方式修正网络。Sasha 不能删除边、添加新边，也不能改变现有边的方向。他唯一能做的事情是修改容量函数 $*c*(*e*)$ 和流函数 $*f*(*e*)$。此外，所有数值都必须保持为非负整数。对流量是否为任意意义下的最大流没有要求。

请找出 Sasha 为使流变得正确而必须对函数 $*f*(*e*)$ 和 $*c*(*e*)$ 进行的最小总修改量。总修改量定义为绝对差之和，即如果新的函数为 $*f*^{ * }(*e*)$ 和 $*c*^{ * }(*e*)$，则总修改量为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d0231fd13acfe49406e89c890aa30b986fdfee4f.png)。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$，$0 ≤ *m* ≤ 100$）——图中节点和边的数量。接下来的 $*m*$ 行中，每行包含一条边的描述，由四个整数 $*u*_{*i*}$、$*v*_{*i*}$、$*c*_{*i*}$ 和 $*f*_{*i*}$ 组成（$1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$，$*u*_{*i*} ≠ *v*_{*i*}$，$0 ≤ *c*_{*i*}, *f*_{*i*} ≤ 1 000 000$）——边的起点编号、终点编号、当前容量和流量值。

编号为 $1$ 的节点是源点，编号为 $*n*$ 的节点是汇点。保证没有边指向源点，也没有边从汇点出发。

给定的图中不含自环，但可能包含重边。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——Sasha 为得到正确的流描述而必须进行的最小总修改量。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，流一开始就是正确的。注意，流并不是最大流，但题目并不要求这一点。

在第二个样例中，唯一一条边上的流量大于其容量。有两种修正方式：将容量增加到 $2$，或者将流量减少到 $1$。

在第三个样例中，进入节点 $2$ 的流量只有 $1$，但从该节点流出的流量为 $2$。一种可行的方案是将第二条边上的流量减少 $1$。

在第四个样例中，存在独立的流循环，但根据定义，这种描述是正确的。
